plan: Ten new items with subskills checked against the bank (a conditional 'at least one girl' idea dropped as a concept repeat of the reduced-sample-space item). 4 hard (square in a semicircle, reversed percent, reflection across y = x + 1, matched pair) / 3 medium / 3 easy.

candidates.subskill: Evaluating an expression at a negative value
candidates.stem: What is the value of 3x² - x when x = -2 ?

A.rationale: -14 negates the correct value, treating the whole expression as negative because x is negative.

hints: Use parentheses when substituting a negative number.

candidates.stem:
The tables below give values of the functions f and g.
x | 1 | 2 | 3
f(x) | 4 | 7 | 10
g(x) | 9 | 5 | 1
What is the value of (f + g)(2) ?

A.rationale: 9 is g(1), read from the wrong column.

C.rationale: 14 doubles f(2) instead of adding g(2).

D.rationale: 35 multiplies f(2) and g(2) instead of adding them.

strategy.explanation: Read both values in the x = 2 column.

candidates.subskill: Base angles of an isosceles triangle
candidates.stem: In isosceles triangle PQR, PQ = PR and the measure of angle P is 40°. What is the measure of angle Q ?
candidates.explanation: The base angles Q and R are equal and sum to 180° - 40° = 140°, so each is 70°.

A.rationale: 40° assumes angle Q equals angle P.

B.rationale: 50° subtracts 40° from 90°, as if the triangle had a right angle.

D.rationale: 140° is the sum of the two base angles.

hints: Which angles are equal when PQ = PR?

strategy.explanation: Mark the equal sides and the angles opposite them.

candidates.remember: Equal sides are opposite equal angles.

candidates.stem: Today is a Tuesday. What day of the week will it be 100 days from today?
candidates.explanation: Days of the week repeat every 7 days. 100 = 7 × 14 + 2, so 100 days from Tuesday is 2 days after Tuesday: Thursday.

A.rationale: Wednesday counts only 1 extra day, as if 100 = 7 × 14 + 1.

C.rationale: Friday counts 3 extra days, miscounting the remainder.

D.rationale: Saturday counts 4 extra days, adding the remainder of 100 ÷ 12 instead of 100 ÷ 7.

hints: What is the remainder when 100 is divided by 7?

strategy.explanation: Every 7 days it is Tuesday again.

candidates.stem: A survey of 120 students recorded whether each student has a part-time job and whether each plays a sport. Of the 120 students, 45 have a job, 50 play a sport, and 20 have a job and play a sport. How many students neither have a job nor play a sport?
candidates.explanation: Students with a job or a sport: 45 + 50 - 20 = 75. Those with neither: 120 - 75 = 45.

A.rationale: 25 is the number who have a job but do not play a sport.

B.rationale: 35 = 120 - 45 - 50 + 10 subtracts both groups and adds back only half the overlap.

D.rationale: 75 is the number who have a job, play a sport, or both.

hints: Fill in a 2 × 2 table, starting with the 20 in the overlap cell.
candidates.remember: Subtract the overlap once when combining two groups.

candidates.stem: A shipping company charges $4.00 for the first pound and $1.50 for each additional pound or fraction of a pound. What is the cost to ship a package that weighs 5.3 pounds?
candidates.explanation: After the first pound, 4.3 pounds remain. Any fraction counts as a full pound, so that is 5 additional pounds: $4.00 + 5 × $1.50 = $11.50.

A.rationale: $7.95 = $1.50 × 5.3 applies the additional-pound rate to the whole weight.

hints: How many additional pounds are charged, counting any fraction as a whole pound?

candidates.stem: A square is inscribed in a semicircle of radius 5 so that one side of the square lies along the diameter and the other two vertices lie on the arc. What is the area of the square?
candidates.explanation: Let the side be s. The square is centered on the diameter, so a top vertex is s/2 from the center horizontally and s up. Then (s/2)² + s² = 5², so (5/4)s² = 25 and s² = 20.

A.rationale: 12.5 = 25/2 halves the area of a square whose side is the radius.

C.rationale: 25 assumes the side of the square equals the radius.

D.rationale: 50 is the area of a square inscribed in the full circle.

hints: Draw a radius from the center to an upper vertex of the square.
The center of the semicircle is the midpoint of the square's bottom side.

strategy.explanation: Use a right triangle with legs s/2 and s.

candidates.remember: Inscribed figures: draw a radius to a vertex and use the Pythagorean theorem.

author_checklist.hardness: The key setup (center at the midpoint of the base, legs s/2 and s) is not obvious, and the full-circle answer 50 is a strong trap.

candidates.stem: The price of Model A is 25% more than the price of Model B. The price of Model B is what percent less than the price of Model A?
candidates.explanation: Let B = 100, so A = 125. B is 25 less than A, and 25/125 = 20%.

B.rationale: 25% assumes the percent difference is the same in both directions.

D.rationale: 80% is B as a percent of A, not how much less B is.

hints: Pick a price for Model B, such as 100.
candidates.remember: Percent difference depends on the base: divide by the reference amount.

author_checklist.hardness: The symmetric answer 25% catches most quick solvers; the base changes when the comparison is reversed.

candidates.subskill: Reflection across a line not through the origin
candidates.stem: In the standard (x,y) coordinate plane, point P(4, 1) is reflected across the line y = x + 1. What are the coordinates of the image of P ?
candidates.explanation: The image P' is such that the line y = x + 1 is the perpendicular bisector of PP'. The segment PP' has slope -1: from (4, 1) the image is (4 - t, 1 + t). Its midpoint (4 - t/2, 1 + t/2) lies on y = x + 1: 1 + t/2 = (4 - t/2) + 1, so t = 4 and P' = (0, 5). Check: the midpoint (2, 3) is on the line.

B.rationale: (1, 4) reflects across y = x, ignoring the + 1.

C.rationale: (2, 3) is the midpoint of P and its image, the point on the line.

hints: The mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of the segment from P to its image.
Move along slope -1 from P until you reach the line, then go the same distance again.

strategy.explanation: Plot the line and P, then move perpendicular to the line.

candidates.remember: Reflection: the mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of the point and its image.

author_checklist.hardness: The swap-coordinates rule works only for y = x; the shifted line requires the perpendicular-bisector setup.

candidates.subskill: Probability of selecting a matched pair
candidates.stem: Four married couples attend a meeting. Two of the 8 people are chosen at random to give a presentation. What is the probability that the two people chosen are married to each other?
candidates.explanation: There are C(8, 2) = 28 equally likely pairs, and 4 of them are married couples: 4/28 = 1/7. (Equivalently, once the first person is chosen, 1 of the remaining 7 is that person's spouse.)

A.rationale: 1/28 is the probability of choosing one particular couple.

B.rationale: 1/8 uses 8 people instead of the 7 remaining after the first choice.

D.rationale: 1/4 treats the 4 couples as the only possible outcomes.

hints: After the first person is chosen, how many people remain, and how many of them are that person's spouse?

strategy.explanation: Fix the first person, then find the chance the second is the spouse.

candidates.remember: Fix the first choice, then count favorable second choices.

author_checklist.hardness: Requires seeing that any first person works and only the spouse completes a couple; 1/28 and 1/8 are tempting.
